title: Trump Rolls Back Fuel Rules: What It Means for Cars
summary: Imagine if your family's car could go farther on a gallon of gas. That's what fuel economy rules are about. Under President Biden, the rules said cars and light trucks should average about 50.4 miles per gallon by 2031. That's like driving from New York City to Philadelphia on one gallon of gas! But on Saturday, President Donald Trump announced he is rolling back those rules. He called Biden's plan an "EV mandate" — even though there is no law that says you must buy an electric car. Trump said the new standards will "take the waste out of building cars in America" and mean "LOWER PRICES" for families. In December 2025, he proposed a new target of about 34.5 miles per gallon by 2031 — more than 30 percent lower than Biden's rule. The rules are called CAFE standards, and they've been around since 1975. They work by making carmakers balance gas guzzlers with efficient cars. Trump didn't give exact numbers this time, but his Transportation Secretary said an announcement is "COMING MONDAY." Supporters say this helps car companies and buyers. Critics worry it will increase pollution and make the U.S. fall behind other countries in electric cars.
why_it_matters: The rules decide what cars your family can buy, how much gas they use, and how much the air around your school and neighborhood is polluted.

background_read: The U.S. made its first big fuel-saving rules in 1975, after an oil shortage made gas prices jump and people wanted cars that used less.
Since then, presidents have changed the numbers up and down: some set stricter goals to cut pollution, and others loosen them to keep car prices low.
Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) is now loosening the rules again, and he says an electric-car rule exists — but no law actually forces people to buy an electric car.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, his Transportation Secretary, and both supporters and critics of the change.

WHAT: Trump announced he is rolling back the fuel economy rules that wanted cars and light trucks to average about 50.4 miles per gallon by 2031, moving toward a target of about 34.5 miles per gallon.
WHERE: These are national rules for the whole United States, covering cars and light trucks; the announcement is expected Monday.
WHY: Supporters say it takes waste out of building cars and brings lower prices for families, while critics say it will add pollution and slow the U.S. in electric cars.

perspectives.description: They say weaker rules mean cheaper cars and less pressure on American carmakers, so families pay less.
They worry the change means more pollution from gas guzzlers and that the U.S. will fall behind other countries making electric cars.
They note that these fuel rules have flipped back and forth between presidents for decades, so each new leader sets the number they prefer.
